grammar.pt: <compared item> + 比 + <reference item> + (多 / 少) + <verb> + <quantity phrase>
grammar.ds: Difference in how much action or quantity occurs.

ex.translation: I drink one more cup of tea than you.

grammar.ds: Even greater degree relative to the reference; not fairly-还.

ex.translation: Today is even colder than yesterday.

grammar.ds: Action occurs earlier/later by a stated interval.

ex.translation: I came back ten minutes later than you.

grammar.ds: Deny a greater degree; does not necessarily assert a lesser degree.

ex.translation: Today is not colder than yesterday.

grammar.ds: Same in a contextually understood respect.

ex.translation: This book is the same as that book.

grammar.ds: Equal degree of the stated quality.

ex.translation: I am just as busy as you.

grammar.ds: High degree after an adjective, not manner after a verb.

ex.translation: It is very cold today.

grammar.ds: A quality or state itself serves as subject.

ex.translation: Being too late is not good.

grammar.ds: Relatively or fairly; no explicit comparison object follows 比较.

ex.translation: This method is fairly simple.

grammar.ds: Other members; understood nouns can be omitted.

ex.translation: I want to watch another movie.

grammar.ds: Neither extreme, in conventional paired descriptions; not every 不A不B idiom.

ex.translation: This shop is neither big nor small.

grammar.pr: bù dàn + <first clause>, ér qiě + <stronger clause>
grammar.ds: Strengthen an added point; subject position follows shared versus distinct subjects.

ex.translation: He not only likes tea, but also likes coffee.

grammar.ds: Rhetorical reminder expecting agreement with the underlying positive statement.

ex.translation: Isn’t he Chinese?

grammar.ds: 不一会儿 introduces an event after a short interval.

ex.translation: After a little while, the teacher came.

grammar.ds: An amount smaller than expected.

ex.translation: He is only twenty years old.

grammar.ds: Approximately an amount; lexical 不 is neutral here.

ex.translation: This road is about one hundred meters long.

grammar.pt: 除了 + <exception> + 以外，<remaining group> + 都 + <predicate>
grammar.pr: chú le + <exception> + yǐ wài, <remaining group> + dōu + <predicate>
grammar.ds: Exclude an exception before a universal statement; 以外 optional.

ex.translation: Except for my younger brother, we all drink coffee.

grammar.pt: 除了 + <included item> + 以外，<subject> + (还 / 也) + <predicate>
grammar.pr: chú le + <included item> + yǐ wài, <subject> + (hái / yě) + <predicate>
grammar.ds: Inclusive addition of a fact or participant; 以外 may be omitted.

ex.translation: Besides tea, he also drinks coffee.

grammar.ds: 的话 follows the condition; not literal speech.

ex.translation: If you have time, then call me.

grammar.ds: Contrast; 可 is conjunction kě, not the possibility modal.

ex.translation: I want to go, but I do not have time today.

grammar.ds: Mark the starting boundary explicitly with 起.

ex.translation: Starting tomorrow, I will work at home.

grammar.ds: Approximate quantity rather than probability of a whole statement.

ex.translation: About ten students came today.

grammar.ds: Present something as expected or unsurprising.

ex.translation: Of course you can come.

grammar.pt: (东方 / 南方 / 西方 / 北方) + <location predicate>
grammar.pr: (dōng fāng / nán fāng / xī fāng / běi fāng) + <location predicate>
grammar.ds: Direction or region as a nominal; 西方 need not mean Western countries.

ex.translation: There are many schools in the south.

grammar.ds: Scope an evaluation to a person, group or relevant entity.

ex.translation: For children, this question is too difficult.

grammar.ds: Time since an event ended; not duration of the action itself.

ex.translation: It has been two days since Dad left the hospital.

grammar.ds: Specialist or expert suffix in established words, not freely productive.

ex.translation: She is a musician.

grammar.ds: It is time to act; not only general advice.

ex.translation: It is time to sleep.

grammar.ds: Ground a decision or inference in a stated basis.

ex.translation: According to the map, the airport is north of the school.

grammar.ds: Greater degree relative to an explicit or understood baseline.

ex.translation: It is colder today.

grammar.ds: Introduce a discourse topic; not the target of an attitude.

ex.translation: About this question, we can talk tomorrow.

grammar.ds: Fairly or acceptably; distinct from still and additive 还.

ex.translation: This bag is fairly cheap.

grammar.pr: huò zhě + <option clause>, huò zhě + <alternative clause>
grammar.ds: Present alternative propositions rather than ask a direct choice.

ex.translation: You can either take the subway or take a taxi.

grammar.ds: Only this member or amount; scope follows 就.

ex.translation: Only he can drive.

grammar.ds: Judging from available indications; not established certainty.

ex.translation: Apparently he is not coming today.

grammar.ds: Familiar surname address; context governs appropriateness, not literal age alone.

ex.translation: Lao Wang is taking the day off today.

grammar.pt: <place noun> + (东 / 南 / 西 / 北)
grammar.ds: Cardinal direction relative to a place.

ex.translation: There is a restaurant east of the school.

grammar.pt: <place> + <appearance verb> + <result or direction complement> + 了 + <quantity phrase> + <entity>
grammar.pr: <place> + <appearance verb> + <result or direction complement> + le + <quantity phrase> + <entity>
grammar.ds: Introduce entities appearing at a location; aspect and complements must fit.

ex.translation: Two people walked in through the doorway.

grammar.ds: Entities cease to be present; not a static absence statement.

ex.translation: Two people walked out of the classroom.

grammar.ds: Every individual member; restricted reduplication such as 个个 or 张张.

ex.translation: Every household has a television.

grammar.ds: Two adjacent expressions identify the same referent.

ex.translation: My friend Lao Wang is taking the day off today.

grammar.ds: In the middle of one region or between specified referents.

ex.translation: There is a bookstore between the two schools.

grammar.ds: 班 counts scheduled departures or services; not the class-group noun.

ex.translation: There are two train services today.

grammar.pt: <number> + <measure word> + <same number> + <same measure word> + 地 + <verb phrase>
grammar.pr: <number> + <measure word> + <same number> + <same measure word> + de + <verb phrase>
grammar.ds: Successive equal groups, often one by one; 地 may be omitted.

ex.translation: The students came in one by one.

grammar.ds: Conventional adjacent-number approximation; not unrestricted concatenation.

ex.translation: I waited three or four minutes.

grammar.ds: 所 counts institutions such as schools, not all buildings.

ex.translation: There are two schools here.

grammar.ds: Bowlfuls/platefuls; explicit borrowed measures, not container objects.

ex.translation: We ordered two bowls of rice.

grammar.ds: Alternatives in a statement, not a direct choice question.

ex.translation: For dinner, I want bread or rice.

grammar.ds: Common modifier order; scope and modifier type can alter placement.

ex.translation: My older brother's two old pieces of clothing are both too small.

grammar.ds: Passive event with or without an agent; not an unbounded bare verb.

ex.translation: My phone was taken away by my younger brother.

grammar.ds: Overwhelming degree with compatible predicates, not literal damage.

ex.translation: I was swamped today.

grammar.ds: Extreme degree; 极 is a complement, 了 not past tense.

ex.translation: This dish is absolutely delicious.

grammar.ds: Correct or qualify an apparent situation.

ex.translation: She isn't a teacher; she's actually a doctor.

grammar.ds: Person in a role or organization; use established combinations.

ex.translation: My older sister is a server.

grammar.ds: Hypothetical condition and result; not automatic future tense.

ex.translation: If it rains tomorrow, we'll take a taxi.

grammar.ds: Cause an identifiable object to follow a specified path.

ex.translation: Please put the book in.

grammar.ds: Affect an identifiable object with a bounded result; not a bare action.

ex.translation: She finished the homework.

grammar.ds: Specify the object's resulting condition with 得.

ex.translation: I cleaned the room very thoroughly.

grammar.ds: Transfer a known object; 给 omission depends on the verb.

ex.translation: I lent the book to a coworker.

grammar.ds: Place or move an identifiable object; specify its resulting location.

ex.translation: I put the book on the table.

grammar.ds: Required action; negate necessity with 不必/不用, not simple 不必须.

ex.translation: You have to leave now.

grammar.ds: No need to act; 不必 explicitly introduced, not a prohibition.

ex.translation: You don't need to answer now.

grammar.ds: Emphatically correct a competing judgement; 呢 optional, tone context-sensitive.

ex.translation: "Are you tired?" "Me? I'm not tired at all."

grammar.ds: Nearly reaches completion; not necessarily fully done.

ex.translation: We've almost finished our homework.

grammar.ds: Probable inference, not confirmed fact.

ex.translation: He's probably at school.

grammar.ds: Action across many places, not toward one destination.

ex.translation: The child runs around everywhere.

grammar.ds: Have to; stressed děi, not complement-linking de.

ex.translation: I have to go to the bank.

grammar.ds: Ought to act; not automatically a scheduled turn.

ex.translation: You ought to rest more.

grammar.ds: Action occurred very recently relative to the reference time.

ex.translation: I just got home.

grammar.ds: An impression rather than verified knowledge.

ex.translation: He seems very busy.

grammar.ds: Almost reaches a state or limit; preserve the predicate's polarity.

ex.translation: We were almost home.

grammar.ds: Insist on exactly this judgement or intention, often against an alternative.

ex.translation: They can all go; I'm not going.

grammar.pr: <subject> + (kàn qǐ lai / kàn shang qu) + <adjective phrase>
grammar.ds: Explicit appearance frames, not literal looking upward.

ex.translation: This restaurant looks very clean.

grammar.ds: Immediately or very soon.

ex.translation: I'll be right back.

grammar.ds: Unspecified person/thing in a licensing context; not every modal or negation permits it.

ex.translation: I didn't buy anything.

grammar.ds: A whole proposition serves as subject of the main judgement.

ex.translation: It would be more convenient if you came tomorrow.

grammar.ds: Emphatic opinion or assurance; not focus on a past event's circumstances.

ex.translation: This method is the right one.

grammar.ds: Repeat the verb to accommodate both its object and complement.

ex.translation: You write characters very well.

grammar.ds: Need to act; distinguish taking a required thing as object.

ex.translation: You need to rest more.

grammar.ds: Strong certainty about a proposition, not proof of it.

ex.translation: You must be tired.

grammar.ds: In a short while; not action duration after the verb.

ex.translation: I'll be back in a little while.

grammar.ds: State or activity persists throughout an interval.

ex.translation: He's been working at home the whole time.

grammar.ds: Advice or reasonable expectation, not guaranteed occurrence.

ex.translation: You should drink more water.

grammar.ds: Repetition presented as recurring or realized; contrast future-oriented 再.

ex.translation: He's late again.

grammar.ds: Willingness or readiness to agree, not future tense.

ex.translation: She's willing to help me.

grammar.ds: Ask how an action is performed.

ex.translation: How do you make this dish?

grammar.ds: Merely this, limiting scope; not the contrastive but-use.

ex.translation: I just want to ask one question.

grammar.ds: Restrict the action or its object; 只 takes third tone.

ex.translation: I only drank one cup of water.

grammar.ds: Event finally occurs after waiting or difficulty.

ex.translation: We finally got home.

grammar.ds: Habitually or invariably; complaints may use contextual exaggeration.

ex.translation: He always forgets to bring his phone.

grammar.ds: Neutral-tone noun suffix in established words; not diminutive by default.

ex.translation: This car is very new.

grammar.ds: Especially high degree; not the adjective meaning unusual.

ex.translation: It's especially cold today.

grammar.ds: Not until this time, later than expected.

ex.translation: He didn't get home until ten at night.

grammar.ds: Quite or rather; final 的 commonly accompanies this evaluation.

ex.translation: This pair of shoes is quite expensive.

grammar.ds: 不怎么样 gives an unimpressed evaluation; not a how-question.

ex.translation: This restaurant isn't very good.

grammar.ds: Bring forth or identify a result, not literal outward motion.

ex.translation: I've already figured out a solution.

grammar.ds: Successfully attain the action's goal, not merely attempt it.

ex.translation: I managed to buy a ticket.

grammar.ds: Can/cannot achieve the result; neutral 得, citation 不.

ex.translation: I can understand this character.

grammar.ds: Count complete passes from beginning to end.

ex.translation: I've read this book twice all the way through.

grammar.ds: Mouthful actions; distinct from counting household members.

ex.translation: The water was too hot, so I only took one sip.

grammar.ds: Count utterances, calls or other vocal sounds.

ex.translation: He laughed twice.

grammar.ds: Evoke or bring something into a resulting state; lexicalized combinations only.

ex.translation: I remembered my mom.

grammar.ds: Activity starts; distinct from literal rising.

ex.translation: Everyone started laughing.

grammar.ds: Achieve attachment, closure or contact; lexical verb compatibility matters.

ex.translation: Please close the door.

grammar.ds: Begin an activity or enter an engaged state; compatible verbs only.

ex.translation: As soon as they met, they got chatting.

grammar.ds: Reject or challenge the action; not a neutral request for its object.

ex.translation: Why are you crying? It's okay.

grammar.ds: Retain or set something down as a result; not literal downward travel.

ex.translation: I wrote down your name.

grammar.ds: Activity persists through an interval to the reference point.

ex.translation: This job is hard, but he kept at it.

grammar.ds: Continue an action onward; not literal downward motion.

ex.translation: Stop crying and keep talking.

grammar.ds: First action or posture accompanies the main action; shared subject.

ex.translation: He runs while listening to music.

grammar.ds: Secure or hold a result with a compatible verb.

ex.translation: I've got this name memorized now.

grammar.ds: Resulting removal or departure, not merely the act of walking.

ex.translation: He took my book away.

grammar.ds: Compact completion-then sequence; 就 optional and 了 need not mark past time.

ex.translation: He went home as soon as class ended.

grammar.ds: An activity itself serves as subject.

ex.translation: Studying Chinese is interesting.

grammar.ds: Act for an intended purpose; success is not asserted.

ex.translation: I'm skipping a movie tonight for tomorrow's exam.

grammar.ds: Act for someone's benefit or on their behalf.

ex.translation: I bought coffee for you.

grammar.ds: Cause of an emotion or reaction, not a beneficiary.

ex.translation: I'm worried because of this matter.

grammar.ds: Every possible member or option, not an actual question.

ex.translation: You can eat whatever you want.

grammar.ds: Repeated wh-expression links matching choices; clause position follows each role.

ex.translation: I'll go wherever you want to go.

grammar.ds: Chronological sequence; can narrate completed actions.

ex.translation: Wash your hands first, then eat.

grammar.ds: Ordered planned actions; not necessarily already performed.

ex.translation: Rest first, then get back to work.

grammar.ds: Orient movement toward a direction; not an addressee.

ex.translation: He walked toward the doorway.

grammar.ds: Direct speech, learning or a request toward a person.

ex.translation: You can ask the teacher questions.

grammar.ds: 一般来说 marks a generalization that allows exceptions.

ex.translation: Generally speaking, the north is colder than the south in winter.

grammar.pr: yī biān + <first action>, yī biān + <second action>
grammar.ds: Concurrent activities that can realistically overlap.

ex.translation: She does her homework while listening to music.

grammar.pt: 一点儿 + 也 + 不 + <adjective or attitude predicate>
grammar.pr: yī diǎn r + yě + bù + <adjective or attitude predicate>
grammar.ds: Not at all; degree negation rather than counting objects.

ex.translation: I'm not tired at all.

grammar.ds: Insistent instruction or resolve to carry out an action.

ex.translation: Be sure to come tomorrow.

grammar.ds: Total across all relevant members or amounts.

ex.translation: We bought three books in total.

grammar.pt: 一会儿 + <first action>，一会儿 + <next action>
grammar.pr: yī huì r + <first action>, yī huì r + <next action>
grammar.ds: Alternate actions or states over short intervals.

ex.translation: The child laughs one moment and cries the next.

grammar.pt: 一 + <measure word> + <noun> + (也 / 都) + (不 / 没) + <verb phrase>
grammar.ds: Not even one; choose 不/没 by event and aspect.

ex.translation: I didn't eat even one apple.

grammar.ds: Somewhat, often undesirably; not the pronoun meaning some.

ex.translation: This question is a bit hard.

grammar.ds: Both compatible qualities, not either-or alternatives.

ex.translation: The food at this restaurant is both cheap and tasty.

grammar.ds: Both compatible activities occur; simultaneity is not required.

ex.translation: He sang and jumped around.

grammar.ds: Increasing degree over time without a separate comparison target.

ex.translation: The weather is getting colder and colder.

grammar.ds: Increasing degree of an attitude or ability, not any arbitrary action.

ex.translation: She likes Chinese more and more.

grammar.ds: Two degrees covary; not simply successive actions.

ex.translation: The more you practice, the better you write.

grammar.ds: Under circumstances or influence, not physical position below.

ex.translation: At the teacher's request, everyone quieted down.

grammar.ds: Scope a claim to a particular respect, not a physical surface.

ex.translation: When it comes to work, he's very conscientious.

grammar.ds: Limit a judgement to a person's viewpoint.

ex.translation: In my view, this book is very interesting.

grammar.ds: Within an ongoing process or context.

ex.translation: He works very hard during the competition.

grammar.pt: 在 + <time or event> + (以前 / 以后 / 前 / 后)，<statement>
grammar.pr: zài + <time or event> + (yǐ qián / yǐ hòu / qián / hòu), <statement>
grammar.ds: Before/after a reference event or time; 在 may be omitted.

ex.translation: After the exam, we went to eat.

grammar.ds: A sufficient condition within the stated context.

ex.translation: As long as you come, I'll be happy.

grammar.ds: Necessary condition, not a guarantee of the result.

ex.translation: I'll only know if you tell me.
